# The reason is MANDATORY — tests/no-upstream-regression-gate.sh fails (exit 2) on an
# entry with an empty reason, and prints every reason it honours.
#
# POLICY (2026-09-11). Zene Studio is a product, not an upstream patch series. A blanket
# ban on touching inherited code would forbid exactly the work a DAW needs — you cannot
# implement plugin delay compensation without changing the mixer. What this file forbids
# is *undeclared* divergence: a behavioural change to an inherited file that nobody wrote
# down. Every entry here is deliberate and reviewed; anything NOT listed is still a
# violation. Keep each change minimal and local, and ship a test beside it (the gate's
# rule: fork-NEW fixes need a regression test in the same change).
#
# Reasons reference the task/commit that made the change, so a future rebase onto upstream
# can see what this repo owes. When upstream's copy of a file is taken wholesale, delete
# its entry here — an entry that no longer differs from the base is dead weight.
#

# --- fix(control-undo): the four paths of the undo SIGSEGV (2026-09-12) ---------
# docs/CONTROL-UNDO-CONNECTION-DROP.md. `control.undo` unwinds the engine's own
# ProjectJournal - the same stack the GUI's Ctrl+Z unwinds - and restoring a Song
# checkpoint tears the track container down and rebuilds it. Four reads of
# PatternTrack's static registry used QMap::operator[], which INSERTS a zero for an
# absent key: the destructor of the old track erases its entry and then the GUI's
# PatternTrackView::close() (reached through the destroyedTrack() signal) reads it.
# The ghost entry - keyed by the dead track's address, which the allocator then
# hands to its replacement - makes the replacement derive its pattern number from
# s_infoMap.size() and get the wrong one, leaving an index with no track; the
# pattern combobox then dereferenced the nullptr: SIGSEGV on the UI thread, the
# process gone, and every client connection with it. Every change below is a read
# (QMap::value()) where a lookup-with-insert was. value() returns the same int as
# operator[] for a registered track, so no registered-track behaviour changes; the
# only behaviour that goes away is the fabricated entry. The invariant the four
# changes restore: only PatternTrack's constructor creates a registry entry, and
# only its destructor erases one.

# --- fix(control-undo): the release-configuration SIGSEGV after the reply -----
# docs/UNDO-RELEASE-CONFIG.md. `transport.set_tempo {"bpm":128}` then `control.undo`
# on an untouched new project (the default project: an instrument, sample, pattern
# and automation track) replies ok and then dies with SIGSEGV, 8 of 8 runs, on the
# release configuration only. The undo restores a Song checkpoint, whose
# TrackContainer::loadSettings tears the container down and rebuilds it
# (clearAllTracks()). It deleted the TRACKS while their views were still up.
# A TrackView sets Qt::WA_DeleteOnClose and closes itself from the track's
# destroyedTrack() signal, so the view is deleted from a DEFERRED event, i.e.
# after the track it views is gone; ~InstrumentTrackView() then reads the dead
# model (`delete model()->m_midiPort.m_readablePortsMenu`). From the crash
# frame: SIGSEGV at si_addr 0x308 with rdi 0 - `model()`'s dynamic_cast returns
# nullptr on the destroyed track and the null base is dereferenced at the member's
# offset. The order the rest of the tree keeps is view-then-track
# (TrackContainerView::deleteTrackView(), Song::clearProject() clearing the editor
# views first); the serialization-restore path was the one that did not announce
# itself. The change is that announcement plus the slot that answers it: no view
# or track behaviour is altered on any other path.

# --- 040/focus-desk (UI plan §9.4, 2026-09-21) ------------------------------
# One inherited GUI class, two null tests. The Focus Desk mounts an editor by
# taking it out of the QMdiSubWindow that wraps it, which is what Qt's
# setWidget(nullptr) is for; LMMS's own SubWindow then holds no widget. Its
# show/hide and its detach check both read widget() unconditionally, so the
# first hide() of an emptied window segfaults (measured: SIGSEGV at
# SubWindow.cpp:219 <- SubWindow::setVisible <- FocusDeskPane::claim, on the
# real binary with ui/focusdesk=1). Two neighbouring members of the same class,
# adjustTitleBar() (line 141) and detach() (line 319), already test widget() for
# null, so the file's own convention is that a subwindow may be empty and these
# two just missed it. No behaviour changes when a widget is present: the same
# branches run, in the same order. Regression test beside it -
# FocusDeskPaneTest::claimingOutOfAProductSubWindowLeavesItSafeToHide, which
# takes a widget out of a real SubWindow and hides and shows it again.

cmake/nsis/CMakeLists.txt	030/cf2 Windows packaging fix, the windows-arm64 Package failure: the inherited 64-bit branch of cmake/nsis/CMakeLists.txt injected the install directory through CPACK_NSIS_DEFINES ('SET(CPACK_INSTALL_FIX "$PROGRAMFILES64\\${CPACK_PACKAGE_INSTALL_DIRECTORY}\\")' then 'InstallDir ${CPACK_INSTALL_FIX}'), which reaches makensis unquoted and space-separated and aborts every Windows NSIS package instantly -- 'InstallDir expects 1 parameters, got 2. / Error in script ".../project.nsi" on line 49 -- aborting creation process' -- reported by CPack only as 'Problem running NSIS command' + 'Problem compressing the directory' because makensis's own text goes to _CPack_Packages/<system>/NSIS/NSISOutput.log, which no step captured (job 103647387841 / run 34728692245; the windows-arm64 Package step has never succeeded in any run). The 64-bit Program Files root now rides CPACK_NSIS_INSTALL_ROOT, which CPack's NSIS template substitutes into its own quoted InstallDir line and also uses for the repair/uninstall comparison, so $INSTDIR is consistent. Reproduced and fixed end to end on this box against Ubuntu nsis 3.09, the same makensis the mingw64 job packages with. The file is read only when LMMS_BUILD_WIN32 (cmake/CMakeLists.txt:26), so no other platform's CPack configuration changes.

The writer emits the attribute ONLY for a reversed source (`if (m_sample.reversed()) _this.setAttribute("reversed", "true")`), so on restore its absence is an explicit "plays forwards" and not "no change" - the reader used to do nothing at all unless the attribute was present, then call setReversed(true), so a restore over a live clip the GUI had since reversed (SampleClipView's reverse toggle journals no step of its own) left that clip reversed. src/core/SampleDecoder.cpp	import detection (feature row 34) found a real defect on the refusal path: decodeSampleDS() read Engine::audioEngine()->outputSampleRate() with no null check, so ANY file the decoders before it cannot read SIGSEGVs the process in a context that never brought the audio subsystem up (measured: the registered ImportDetectionTest, which analyses a path that does not exist, segfaulted at address 0x288 inside Engine::audioEngine()). src/core/SampleDecoder.cpp	import detection (feature row 34) found a real defect on the refusal path: decodeSampleDS() read Engine::audioEngine()->outputSampleRate() with no null check, so ANY file the decoders before it cannot read SIGSEGVs the process in a context that never brought the audio subsystem up (measured: the registered ImportDetectionTest, which analyses a path that does not exist, segfaulted at address 0x288 inside Engine::audioEngine()). The fix is one guard: with no engine there is no rate to synthesise a DS file at, so the decoder REFUSES (std::nullopt) instead of dereferencing null. It can only change behaviour in a process where the DS decoder could never have worked anyway; a normal session has an engine and is byte-for-byte unchanged.

src/core/SampleDecoder.cpp	import detection (feature row 34) found a real defect on the refusal path: decodeSampleDS() read Engine::audioEngine()->outputSampleRate() with no null check, so ANY file the decoders before it cannot read SIGSEGVs the process in a context that never brought the audio subsystem up (measured: the registered ImportDetectionTest, which analyses a path that does not exist, segfaulted at address 0x288 inside Engine::audioEngine()). The fix is one guard: with no engine there is no rate to synthesise a DS file at, so the decoder REFUSES (std::nullopt) instead of dereferencing null. It can only change behaviour in a process where the DS decoder could never have worked anyway; a normal session has an engine and is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Journalled, each write reached AutomatableModel::setValue -> addJournalCheckPoint (src/core/AutomatableModel.cpp:317) and pushed an undo step for an assignment nobody asked to undo. On the two Linux CI runners the MIDI client is the RAW MidiDummy fallback (no ALSA sequencer: src/core/AudioEngine.cpp:1036 with include/MidiClient.h:145, isRaw() true), so the save-time flip put ONE step on the stack for render.render, bounce.in_place and project.save - all three not_mutating (src/core/ControlReversibilityTableSnapshot.cpp:73 for project.save) - and ControlFreezeCommandsTranscript failed with the committed assertion verbatim: reproduced on this box with MIDIDEV=/dev/null (exit 1 before this change, exit 0 after) and 0 of 41 trace entries differing from the CI job; macOS (include/MidiApple.h:113) and Windows (include/MidiWinMM.h:113) clients are not raw, which is exactly why only the Linux jobs were red. Precedent in this tree for a model that is deliberately not journalled: src/gui/editors/SongEditor.cpp:250 (zooming), src/gui/editors/AutomationEditor.cpp:115 (tension), src/gui/widgets/AutomatableButton.cpp:220 (button-group members). NOTHING is dropped to get the zero: the flags are still written with the port by MidiPort::saveSettings (:197-198) and restored by loadSettings (:251-252), and a checkpoint taken on the port itself still carries them as attributes. Held by tests/src/core/UndoBoundsTest.cpp::aDeviceAssignmentIsNotAnUndoStep (the flag still changes, the depth does not move, the value still round-trips) and by the release-gate transcript tests/control-freeze-commands-transcript.py, which is the test that fails without it.; 0.3.0 MIDI controller auto-reconnection (feature-list row 18, OWNER-31 item 7): subscribeReadablePort()/subscribeWritablePort() record (or forget) the binding in the client's MidiReconnect memory by IDENTITY - the client and port NAME - instead of the volatile ALSA address, and ~MidiPort forgets every assignment of a port that is going away. The subscription itself is the same call with one record beside it, so a project that binds nothing behaves exactly as before. Held by tests/src/core/MidiReconnectTest.cpp and tests/control-midi-reconnect.py.; 0.5.0 W4: the MIDI-out frame offset reaches the client (processOutEventAt)

src/tracks/MidiClip.cpp	#645 linked / smart clips (feature row 6, docs/LINKED-CLIPS.md) - three additive changes, none of them a change of what an unlinked clip does: (1) the propagation hook - MidiClip::addNote and both MidiClip::removeNote overloads call ClipLinks::mirrorContent(this) when the clip is a member of a link group (linkId() > 0), which copies this clip's note list onto the group's other members; the call is a no-op for every unlinked clip, which is every clip in every project that does not use the feature, and the mirror itself is re-entrancy-guarded in src/core/ClipLinks.cpp so the members' own entry points cannot mirror back; (2) the clip's non-default attributes reach the element - MidiClip::exportToXML calls the already-inherited Clip::saveClipEdits(), and MidiClip::loadSettings calls Clip::loadClipEdits(), so a MIDI clip's `link` attribute (and the take lane / fades / gain that pair already carried) is written only when it is not the neutral default and read back with a reset-on-absence rule - an unlinked, unedited MIDI clip serialises exactly as it did before this change (invariant I9); (3) MidiClip::loadSettings takes a ClipLinks::MirroringSuspension for the length of the load, because a load pass re-creates each clip in turn and propagating there would write half-loaded content into siblings.; 040/survey-fixes G4 (2026-09-28): addNote quantises to the piano roll only when a GUI exists (headless it dereferenced a null getGUI() - reachable from MidiImport's addNote(n)); with a GUI the behaviour is unchanged; 0.5.0 L07 ED-130 (2026-10-03): a MIDI clip's controller lanes - stored and saved by MidiClip (a metadata child, skipped by the note loop), played once per clip per tick from InstrumentTrack::play (playClipControllers); Luna cluster 4248 (2026-10-06, commit 4218c1e30): MidiClip::clearNotes() gained the same propagation hook - `if (linkId() > 0) { ClipLinks::mirrorContent(this); }` after its emit dataChanged(), so a bulk clear of one member writes the emptied note list onto the group's other members instead of leaving the group diverged; a no-op for unlinked clips, re-entrancy-safe via ClipLinks' g_mirrorDepth (writeContent clears a member before copying onto it), and the load path is unchanged because MidiClip::loadSettings already holds a ClipLinks::MirroringSuspension around its clearNotes() call
